item.title: Salmon Sushi Bake
item.description: Everything I love about a spicy salmon roll, without any of the rolling. Scoop it onto a sheet of seaweed and it disappears fast at a party.

item.title: Kerala Style Nadan Pork Fry (Ularthiyathu)
item.description: A classic Kerala-style dry pork roast in which the pork shines with just enough masala. Finger-licking good. My favorite way to eat it, though, is paired with a crispy dosa: a match made in culinary heaven.

item.title: Rotisserie Chicken, Mushroom & Rice Casserole
item.description: First recipe up: a weeknight casserole built around a rotisserie chicken from the grocery store, which does most of the work for you (leftover rotisserie chicken works just as well).

item.title: Virginia Is for (Marathon) Lovers
item.description:
Another Training Block in the Books

Twenty weeks, give or take, plus a few 20-mile weeks I’d already strung together before the official plan even started. By race day, Garmin had the full picture: 715.74 miles and 114 hours 27 minutes on my feet between June 4th and November 14th. Peak week landed at 51 miles, with a 21-mile long run as the biggest single effort before taper. Over the block, my lactate threshold pace dropped from 8:37/mile to 7:59/mile, and VO2 max ticked up from 45 to 48. Whatever that’s worth on race day (and as you’ll see, it’s not everything), the fitness was clearly there.

item.title: Building Nritya Samarpanam - A Bharatanatyam Arangetram Website
item.description:
Some projects are just work. And then there are the ones that mean something.

This past year my wife Anitha has been preparing for her Arangetram - the formal graduation recital in Bharatanatyam, a classical Indian dance form. Months of early mornings, late evenings, and a kind of dedication I have a deep respect for. When it came time to tell the world about the event, I wanted to do it right. Not just a PDF flyer or a WhatsApp message - a proper website, built with care.

item.title: Lent and a Healthier Me
item.description:
In my adult years, every Lent, I decide to give up meat and alcohol. However, in recent years, I haven’t been able to stick to it. Something always gets in the way i.e. devil wins at pushing his temptations and I end up breaking my Lenten abstinence.

This year was different. Today marks 40 days since I embarked on this alcohol and meat-free journey, and boy, am I glad I did.

item.title: Find Your Starting Line: The Race
item.description:
You have started running regularly. You struggled in the beginning, but as you put in the days, you discover the hidden Kipchoge in you. More walk-run sessions are slowly transitioning into longer stretches of running. You feel you are a couple of months away from your first race, but which race?

How do you find races?

My go-to resource is the Running in the USA website.

It lets you filter by month, region, or specific state, and race distance. Once you find a race close to you or in the city you want to run, look up the race on the site Raceraves. Read race reviews to find out what runners of the previous iteration of the race think about it, focus on what they say about race organization and difficulty.

item.title: Racing the Sunshine State
item.description:
Escaping the Cold

As we transitioned from yellows and browns to gray and white, Northeast America was getting colder by the day. It was time to uphold our Thanksgiving getaway tradition - heading somewhere warmer, which, more often than not, meant Florida. Due to the busy hurricane season of 2024, the west/Gulf coast of Florida was ruled out, which eliminated our favorite vacation spot, Anna Maria Island. After much back-and-forth among friends, we narrowed it down to Melbourne. This city was also conveniently close to the Space Coast Half Marathon in Cocoa Beach.

item.title: My Running Journey: From Zero to Half Marathon
item.description:
I am asked this question or a variation of it quite often.

How to start running from 0?

Getting Started

I am often asked about my running journey.

Before I started, I had no experience running long distances. I only took up running when I turned 40. It took me about two months of training by following freely available training plans online. There are many plans out there, including ones titled "Couch to Half Marathon." I highly recommend checking out Marathon Handbook, whose podcast I regularly listen to and enjoy.

item.title: My Unexpected Journey into Long-Distance Running
item.description:
The Spark That Ignited My Running Journey

I never saw myself as a long-distance runner. In fact, I had never run a continuous kilometer in my life. The only running I had ever done was between wickets while playing cricket many years ago.

That changed when my brother and sister-in-law signed up for a half marathon. Having never run before, they not only enjoyed the training process but also experienced the immense joy of accomplishment after finishing their first race. Their excitement was contagious, and it rubbed off on me.

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.description:
Last updated: November 21, 2026

This is a personal, non-commercial blog. There are no ads, no sponsors, no monetization, and nothing here is ever sold or shared with advertisers. This page explains the little data the site does collect, why, and what you can do about it.

What’s collected

Page views (analytics). This site uses GoatCounter, a privacy-friendly analytics tool that doesn’t use cookies and doesn’t build a profile of you. It records aggregate, anonymous counts — which pages were viewed, roughly where from, what browser — never anything tied to you personally.
